notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded implementation of the official 2025 C++ RTI/encoding/HLAextendableVariantRecord.h class. IEEE 1516.2 §4.14.10.3 defines a discriminant at record offset zero, followed by an HLAinteger32BE encoded_length and the mapped alternative. The discriminant is zero-padded by the smallest amount needed to align encoded_length to its four-octet boundary. The encoded_length holds the alternative's byte length, is zero when no alternative applies, and excludes the padding after it. That post-length padding uses the predefined eight-octet alternative boundary; an alternative with a greater boundary is prohibited. Padding is not added after the alternative. Umbra treats the post-length padding as structural even when encoded_length is zero: the source requires it after encoded_length to align the alternative layout, and this preserves a single length-prefixed layout for successful unknown-alternative skips. The Requirements Lab exports five direct candidate statements with broad clause-4 metadata, but has no individual immutable candidate for Equations (3)/(4) or their Size/V definitions; RL-054 records both the provenance and source-candidate coverage boundaries. The official C++ DataElement header identifies hash() as the mapping hook for discriminants. Umbra uses it as a lookup accelerator and also verifies type plus encoded bytes so a hash collision cannot select a different alternative; this is an implementation safety choice, not a separate standards or conformance result. The raw DataElement* variant operations remain caller-owned borrowed storage exactly as the official header documents, while copy/clone operations use internal copies. FOM-level enumerator ranges and HLAother expansion, model-specific encoder factories, adapter exposure, interoperability, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, and conformance remain outside this bounded slice.
